content: Ciprofloxacin, marketed under the brand name CIPRO®, is an antibiotic belonging to the fluoroquinolone class. It is available in various formulations, including tablets, oral suspension, extended-release tablets (CIPRO XR), and intravenous infusion (CIPRO IV). Important Safety Information About CIPRO CIPRO can cause serious side effects, some of which may be life-threatening. If you experience any of the following, seek medical attention immediately and consult your healthcare provider about whether to continue taking the medication. 1. Tendon Rupture or Tendinitis CIPRO can cause tendon inflammation (tendinitis) or rupture, which may occur in individuals of any age. Tendons are the fibrous tissues that connect muscles to bones. Symptoms of tendon problems include pain, swelling, tears, or inflammation, particularly in the Achilles tendon (back of the ankle), shoulder, hand, or other tendon sites. Risk factors for tendon problems include: Age over 60 years. Concurrent use of corticosteroids. History of kidney, heart, or lung transplantation. Physical activity or exercise. Kidney failure or a history of tendon disorders, such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA). If you experience tendon pain, swelling, or inflammation, stop taking CIPRO and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Avoid physical activity or using the affected area until tendinitis or tendon rupture is ruled out. Tendon rupture can occur during or even months after completing CIPRO treatment. Signs of tendon rupture include: A snapping or popping sound in the tendon area. Bruising following an injury in the tendon area. Inability to move the affected area or bear weight. 2. Worsening of Myasthenia Gravis CIPRO may exacerbate symptoms of myasthenia gravis, a condition characterized by muscle weakness. This can lead to severe muscle weakness or breathing difficulties. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if you experience worsening symptoms. What is CIPRO? CIPRO is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. It is not effective against viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. In children under 18 years of age, CIPRO is generally avoided due to an increased risk of musculoskeletal problems, such as joint pain or swelling. Who Should Not Take CIPRO? Do not take CIPRO if you: Have had a severe allergic reaction to fluoroquinolones or any of the ingredients in CIPRO. Are taking tizanidine (Zanaflex®), as serious side effects may occur. Precautions Before Taking CIPRO Inform your healthcare provider if you: Have a history of tendon problems. Have myasthenia gravis. Have central nervous system (CNS) disorders, such as epilepsy or a history of seizures. Have nerve problems or a family history of QT prolongation (a heart rhythm condition). Have kidney problems, as a dose adjustment may be necessary. Are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. CIPRO passes into breast milk and may harm the baby. Are taking any other medications, including over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or supplements. Certain medications can interact with CIPRO, increasing the risk of side effects. Drug Interactions CIPRO may interact with the following medications: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), which may increase the risk of CNS effects and seizures. Blood thinners (e.g., warfarin). Theophylline, which may cause seizures or breathing problems. Glyburide, which may lead to low blood sugar. Antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, tricyclic antidepressants, and corticosteroids, which may increase the risk of tendon injury or heart rhythm changes. Products containing magnesium, calcium, aluminum, iron, or zinc (e.g., antacids or multivitamins), which can reduce the effectiveness of CIPRO. Take CIPRO at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after these products. How to Take CIPRO Take CIPRO exactly as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Tablets and Oral Suspension: Take twice daily (morning and evening) at the same time each day. Swallow tablets whole without splitting, crushing, or chewing. Shake the oral suspension well for 15 seconds before use. CIPRO XR: Take once daily at the same time each day. Swallow the tablet whole. CIPRO IV: Administered via intravenous infusion over 60 minutes by a healthcare provider. CIPRO can be taken with or without food but should not be taken with dairy products or calcium-fortified juices alone. These can be consumed as part of a meal. Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of fluids. Do not skip doses or stop taking CIPRO prematurely, even if you feel better, unless directed by your healthcare provider. Stopping early may lead to bacterial resistance. What to Avoid While Taking CIPRO Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how CIPRO affects you, as it may cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid excessive sunlight, sunlamps, or tanning beds. CIPRO can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight, leading to severe sunburn or blisters. Use sunscreen and protective clothing if you must be in the sun. Possible Side Effects of CIPRO CIPRO can cause serious side effects, including: Central Nervous System Effects: Seizures, dizziness, hallucinations, restlessness, tremors, anxiety, confusion, depression, paranoia, or suicidal thoughts. Severe Allergic Reactions: Hives, difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, rapid heartbeat, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (liver problems). Heart Rhythm Changes: QT prolongation, which can cause a fast or irregular heartbeat. This risk is higher in the elderly or those with a family history of QT prolongation. Pseudomembranous Colitis: Severe diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and fever, which may occur even months after completing treatment. Peripheral Neuropathy: Nerve damage causing pain, burning, tingling, numbness, or weakness in the arms, hands, legs, or feet. This damage may be permanent. Low Blood Sugar: Severe hypoglycemia, especially when taken with glyburide. Photosensitivity: Increased sensitivity to sunlight, leading to sunburn or skin swelling. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, rash, headache, abdominal discomfort, and vaginal yeast infections. Storage Instructions CIPRO Tablets and Oral Suspension: Store below 86°F (30°C). Do not freeze the oral suspension. Discard any unused suspension after 14 days. CIPRO XR: Store between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep all forms of CIPRO out of reach of children. General Information CIPRO should only be used for the condition it was prescribed for. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar symptoms. For more information, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist. You can also contact Bayer at 1-888-842-2937. Ingredients Active Ingredient: Ciprofloxacin. Inactive Ingredients: Vary by formulation and include substances such as cornstarch, microcrystalline cellulose, magnesium stearate, and titanium dioxide.
